title: RBI Hikes Repo Rate by 25 bps: Your Home Loan EMI Impact

faq.a: A basis point is a unit of measure used in finance to denote a percentage change. One basis point is equal to one-hundredth of one percent (0.01%), so 25 basis points equals 0.25%.

faq.q: Will my home loan interest rate change immediately?
faq.a: For EBLR-linked loans, the change is usually quite swift, often within the next interest reset cycle. For MCLR-linked loans, the change might take longer, as it depends on your loan's specific reset clause and the bank's internal MCLR review cycle.

faq.q: Does this hike affect fixed-rate home loans?
faq.a: No, fixed-rate home loans are not directly impacted by changes in the repo rate as their interest rate is fixed for the entire tenure or a specified period. However, new fixed-rate loans offered by banks may see higher rates.

faq.q: Can I switch from a floating rate to a fixed-rate loan?
faq.a: Yes, many banks offer the option to convert your floating rate loan to a fixed-rate loan. However, fixed rates are typically higher than current floating rates, and there might be conversion charges.

faq.q: Is a home loan balance transfer always a good idea after a rate hike?
faq.a: A balance transfer can be beneficial if the new bank offers a significantly lower interest rate. However, you must factor in processing fees, legal charges, and the time involved to ensure the savings outweigh these costs.

faq.q: How often does the RBI change the repo rate?
faq.a: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee meets at least six times a year, typically every two months, to review the economic situation and decide on policy rates. Changes can occur at any of these meetings or even off-cycle if conditions warrant.
